title: HumanReviewResolution
description: One line of the append-only resolution store (resolutions.jsonl). FR-057b / FR-070 / FR-071 / FR-076. Lines are ONLY ever appended; a changed answer is a NEW line; nothing is edited or removed. Each append is an ATOMIC WHOLE-FILE PUBLISH (read + append line + <store>.tmp + flush + fsync + os.replace) so a crash leaves the old file or the new complete file, never a torn line (audit remediation M3). v2.1: `resolution_id` is now content-bound and `sequence_index` is the sole authority for the currently-applicable record (invariants I1-I6, research §22.2).

run_id.description: run_id of the run that created this resolution.

resolution_id.description: CONTENT-BOUND (M1): sha256(canonical_json({applicability_key, sequence_index, selected}))[:16]. `selected` is the full decision payload ({mode, value} for literal, {order} for reading-order). This is a local-store traceability id for cross-references, NOT a cryptographic integrity digest (whole-file integrity is sha256 of the file; artifact identity is run_id). 16 hex is sufficient because sequence_index alone already makes each record unique within a store.

sequence_index.description: THE AUTHORITY for ordering and 'currently-applicable' (H6). Application invariant I1: unique and STRICTLY INCREASING across the whole store; assigned = max(existing) + 1. The currently-applicable resolution for an applicability_key = the valid record with the GREATEST sequence_index for that key.

supersedes.description: AUDIT LINKAGE ONLY — it does not independently select current state. Application invariants: I2 — when a resolution already exists for this applicability_key, `supersedes` = the resolution_id of the currently-applicable prior record for that key at append time; I3 — null IFF no prior record exists for this key; I4 — a non-null target MUST exist in the store, share this applicability_key, and have a LOWER sequence_index; I5 — the per-key `supersedes` graph is a simple chain (no cycles, forks, or orphans). I6 — the loader FAILS CLOSED for a key whose chain violates I2-I5 (raises the review item fresh; never guesses). Research §22.2.

applicability_key.description: sha256(source_sha256 ⧺ conflict_type ⧺ canonical(page, region, aligned candidate-value set) ⧺ canonical_json(config_subset)) — research §22. A changed context ⇒ key no longer matches ⇒ the stored decision is not replayed or silently reused (FR-071) ⇒ a fresh item.

manually_verified.description: true for mode='entered' (FR-068): verified against the original PDF. For mode='entered' the `value` is the reviewer's CONFIRMED INPUT VERBATIM — no .strip(), Unicode normalization, quote/separator rewrite, BOM stripping, or autocorrect (FR-068 / FR-082). For whitespace/newline-sensitive scripting input the normative path is `review resolve --value-file` (research §22.5).

order.description: A permutation of exactly the review item's segment_ids (FR-069).

candidateEvidence.description: One candidate shown to the reviewer (FR-062a/FR-062d/FR-075). Shared shape reused by the queue and verification schemas.
